tasks.source_read: PMC full text PMC3069146 (author manuscript), as read by the first reader
tasks.extracted: Onset of cannabis use before age 14, against at or after 14, predicted transition to DSM-IV cannabis dependence in the unadjusted model (hazard ratio 2.47, 95% CI 2.0 to 3.1) but went with a lower hazard in the adjusted model (0.63, 95% CI 0.5 to 0.9). The authors write that the higher risk with early onset was mostly explained by the socio-economic, psychiatric and drug-use covariates, so that the transition may not be a consequence of early onset itself but of concomitant psychiatric and substance use disorders, and that people who start later may have more intense patterns of use and greater availability, affordability and acceptance of cannabis in late adolescence.
